answer: Tie each agent's reward to a stake that unlocks slowly, then sample random peers to grade its work blind. A sybil operator who splits one stake into a hundred names gets a hundred thin slices, each too small to matter, and the graders never learn whose work they judge, so no whisper of a deal can steer them. Like yarrow spreading only where its roots hold, influence grows only with real, staked effort, not with a plume of fresh accounts.
